title: Body construction record initialization
summary: Recovered VA 0x438560 (RVA 0x38560), 129 bytes. Original custom thiscall ABI uses ECX for this, XMM1 for scalar, three callee-popped stack arguments, and returns this in EAX. Callers at 0x43a868 and 0x47fdbd confirm this convention. Initializes a 0x88-byte construction record, snapshots sixteen source bytes after owner/descriptor/scalar stores, sets fixed parameters, and invokes matrix64-initialize-basis semantics with only three unit diagonal entries. Bytes 0x75..0x77 are untouched. Portable member method uses a conventional source-level ABI. Accepted references were compared directly to immutable Game.exe bytes.
test_description: 21,296 direct oracle comparisons: 11 scalar bit patterns (signed zeros, finite values, subnormals, infinities, quiet/signaling NaNs), 16 MXCSR rounding/FTZ/DAZ modes, external unaligned source and all 121 overlapping source offsets 0..0x78. Checks entire guarded records, return pointer, explicit scalar/token/matrix bits, untouched padding and guards, MXCSR preservation and FS head after every original call. GCC strict warning build and executable pass; supplied VS2013 compiles implementation under O1, O2 and O2 /Oy-.
known_limits: Exact gameplay meanings of scalar, tokens, vector and parameter fields remain unresolved; names intentionally describe offsets or construction context.
Original optimized XMM1 ABI is exposed only through the GCC test adapter using thiscall plus sseregparm; portable member method does not promise binary ABI compatibility.
Valid readable sixteen-byte source and writable record are required; invalid pointers and hardware fault behavior are not modeled.
Matrix helper semantics are included only as this initializer dependency; no expanded recovery scope or byte-matching credit is claimed.
Local supplied MSVC runs use the provided helper; independent native Windows coordinator validation remains external.
